title: Lumière tout autour de nous
oneGoal: Students will identify different sources of light in their environment and understand that light is needed to see things
decisionPoints: What light sources are most visible and safe for students to observe in the classroom?
Should we start with natural light sources or artificial ones?
Are students ready for simple light/dark comparisons?
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces light as necessary for vision and establishes vocabulary through direct observation
realWorldConnection: How students use different types of lights at home and notice when lights are needed

title: Le soleil - notre grande source de lumière
oneGoal: Students will understand that the sun is our most important source of light and provides heat
decisionPoints: How can we safely observe sunlight without looking directly at the sun?
Should we focus on light or heat properties of the sun first?
Are students ready to understand the sun as both light and heat source?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by focusing on the sun as the primary natural light source while introducing heat connection
realWorldConnection: Understanding why we need the sun for daylight and warmth

title: Ombres magiques
oneGoal: Students will observe how shadows form when objects block light and experiment with making different shadows
decisionPoints: What objects create the clearest, most interesting shadows for young learners?
Should we use flashlights or natural sunlight for shadow experiments?
Are students ready for shadow size and direction observations?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by exploring what happens when light is blocked, introducing scientific observation of shadows
realWorldConnection: Noticing shadows of trees, buildings, and people when walking outside on sunny days

title: Expérience avec les ombres
oneGoal: Students will conduct experiments to discover how shadow size changes when objects move closer or farther from light sources
decisionPoints: What safe objects work best for distance-shadow experiments?
Should we focus on shadow size or shadow clarity changes?
Are students ready for making predictions about shadow changes?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by conducting controlled shadow experiments while introducing prediction and observation skills
realWorldConnection: Understanding why shadows look different at different times of day and different distances from lights

title: Lumières artificielles dans notre maison
oneGoal: Students will identify and compare different artificial light sources used in homes and understand their purposes
decisionPoints: Which artificial light sources are most familiar to students?
Should we compare brightness levels or focus on different purposes?
Are students ready for energy usage discussions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by exploring human-made light sources and their practical applications in daily life
realWorldConnection: Recognizing lamps, overhead lights, flashlights, and other lights students use at home

title: Quand avons-nous besoin de lumière artificielle?
oneGoal: Students will understand when artificial lights are needed and why we use them in winter and at night
decisionPoints: How can we demonstrate the need for artificial light in age-appropriate ways?
Should we focus on seasonal light changes or daily light cycles?
Are students ready for comparing winter and summer light needs?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by connecting artificial light use to seasonal and daily cycles, reinforcing winter theme
realWorldConnection: Understanding why we need more lights on during winter days and why lights are important at night

title: La chaleur du soleil
oneGoal: Students will observe and measure how the sun provides heat and understand that heat comes from the sun's light
decisionPoints: What safe methods can demonstrate solar heat for Grade 1 students?
Should we use thermometers or focus on feeling temperature differences?
Are students ready for simple temperature measurement activities?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by exploring the heat properties of sunlight while introducing temperature observation
realWorldConnection: Feeling how sunshine warms us when we play outside and understanding solar heating

title: D'autres sources de chaleur
oneGoal: Students will identify different sources of heat in their environment and understand that heat can come from many sources
decisionPoints: Which heat sources are safe for students to observe and discuss?
Should we categorize heat sources or focus on identifying them?
Are students ready for comparing natural vs artificial heat sources?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by expanding understanding from solar heat to other heat sources in their environment
realWorldConnection: Identifying heaters, fireplaces, hot water, and other heat sources students encounter daily

title: Garder la chaleur en hiver
oneGoal: Students will understand how insulation works and explore materials that help keep heat in during winter
decisionPoints: What insulation materials are safe and effective for classroom demonstrations?
Should we focus on clothing insulation or building insulation concepts?
Are students ready for insulation effectiveness comparisons?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by exploring how we keep and control heat, introducing insulation concepts for winter survival
realWorldConnection: Understanding why we wear coats and how our homes stay warm in winter

title: Expérience: tester l'isolation
oneGoal: Students will conduct experiments to test which materials are best at keeping things warm
decisionPoints: What safe materials can effectively demonstrate insulation principles?
Should we use ice cubes or warm water for insulation testing?
Are students ready for measuring and comparing insulation effectiveness?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by conducting hands-on insulation experiments while practicing scientific method skills
realWorldConnection: Understanding why different winter clothing works better and how insulation keeps us comfortable

title: Lumière et chaleur des animaux
oneGoal: Students will explore how some animals create their own light or use heat to survive in winter
decisionPoints: Which animal light/heat examples are most accessible to Grade 1 students?
Should we focus on bioluminescence or animal heat adaptations?
Are students ready for comparing animal and human heat strategies?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by exploring biological sources of light and heat, connecting to living things curriculum
realWorldConnection: Learning about fireflies, warm-blooded animals, and how animals stay warm in winter

title: Faire des reflets avec la lumière
oneGoal: Students will discover how mirrors and shiny surfaces reflect light and can redirect light beams
decisionPoints: What reflective surfaces are safe and produce clear reflections for students?
Should we focus on mirror reflections or various reflective materials?
Are students ready for directing reflected light beams?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by exploring how light bounces and moves, introducing reflection principles
realWorldConnection: Understanding how mirrors work and noticing reflections in water, windows, and shiny surfaces

title: Couleurs dans la lumière
oneGoal: Students will observe how white light contains many colors and explore simple light spectrum concepts
decisionPoints: What safe methods can demonstrate light spectrum to young learners?
Should we use prisms, water, or soap bubbles for color demonstrations?
Are students ready for understanding white light composition?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by exploring light properties beyond reflection, introducing color and spectrum concepts
realWorldConnection: Understanding rainbows, soap bubble colors, and why we see different colors in light

title: Notre journal de lumière et chaleur
oneGoal: Students will document their discoveries about light and heat sources through scientific recording and observation logs
decisionPoints: What documentation format works best for Grade 1 scientific recording?
Should we include drawings, measurements, or written observations?
Are students ready for organizing their learning into categories?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by synthesizing all learning into scientific documentation while practicing science communication
realWorldConnection: Learning how scientists keep records of their observations and discoveries

title: Économiser l'énergie lumineuse
oneGoal: Students will understand energy conservation and learn simple ways to save light energy in winter (extension)
decisionPoints: Which energy conservation concepts are appropriate for Grade 1 understanding?
Should we focus on turning off lights or using natural light more?
Are students ready for discussing environmental responsibility?
progression: Extension of Lesson 14 - applies light learning to practical conservation while introducing environmental stewardship
realWorldConnection: Understanding why we turn off lights when not needed and how to use daylight effectively

title: Lumière et chaleur dans d'autres pays
oneGoal: Students will explore how people in different climates use light and heat differently (extension)
decisionPoints: Which global examples best illustrate different light/heat needs?
Should we compare arctic vs tropical heat needs or seasonal differences?
Are students ready for simple geography and climate connections?
progression: Extension of Lesson 15 - broadens perspective on light and heat needs while exploring global diversity
realWorldConnection: Understanding how people in very cold or very hot places meet their light and heat needs

title: Inventer des solutions de chaleur
oneGoal: Students will design simple inventions to solve winter heating problems using their knowledge of heat sources (extension)
decisionPoints: What design challenges are appropriate for Grade 1 problem-solving skills?
Should we focus on personal warming devices or room heating solutions?
Are students ready for invention planning and simple engineering design?
progression: Extension of Lesson 16 - applies heat knowledge to creative problem-solving while introducing design thinking
realWorldConnection: Understanding how inventors create new ways to keep people warm and comfortable

title: Lumière et chaleur pour les plantes d'hiver
oneGoal: Students will investigate how plants need light and heat to survive winter indoors (extension)
decisionPoints: Which plants best demonstrate winter light and heat needs?
Should we focus on houseplants or greenhouse concepts?
Are students ready for plant care experiments?
progression: Extension of Lesson 17 - connects light and heat concepts to plant biology while reinforcing living things needs
realWorldConnection: Understanding how houseplants and greenhouse plants get the light and warmth they need in winter

title: Spectacle de lumière scientifique
oneGoal: Students will create a light demonstration show sharing their discoveries about light sources, shadows, and reflections (extension)
decisionPoints: What light demonstrations are safe for students to perform?
Should we focus on shadow play or light source demonstrations?
Are students ready for teaching others about their discoveries?
progression: Extension of Lesson 18 - culminates learning through performance and teaching while building presentation confidence
realWorldConnection: Learning how scientists share their knowledge through demonstrations and shows

title: Célébration: petits experts en lumière et chaleur
oneGoal: Students will celebrate their learning journey by sharing light and heat knowledge with families through interactive demonstrations (extension)
decisionPoints: How can the celebration showcase each student's understanding of light and heat concepts?
Should we include hands-on experiments or demonstration stations?
What activities best show student growth to families?
progression: Extension of Lesson 19 - celebrates complete unit mastery while building community connections and scientific confidence
realWorldConnection: How sharing scientific knowledge helps families understand light and heat in their daily lives
